extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to a well-known hardcoded value 'field-dispatch-dev-jwt-secret-change-in-production' when process.env.JWT_SECRET is unset. extra.message: POST /api/webhooks/:id/test-delivery takes an arbitrary URL from the 'x-webhook-callback' request header (falling back to the stored webhook URL) and the server fetches it with no host/scheme allowlist or redirect protection. This is a classic SSRF: the value can point at loopback (http://127.0.0.1:...), cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), or internal services. The sibling document-source-verify route enforces an ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist, confirming the control is missing here.

extra.message: POST /api/workers/onboard-account hashes the new worker's password with a bcrypt cost factor taken directly from the request body and defaulting to only 4 rounds (bcrypt.hash(password, costFactor || 4)). 2^4 rounds is trivially brute-forceable, producing weak password hashes for onboarded worker accounts, and an attacker-controlled huge costFactor value can also stall the event loop (bcryptjs is synchronous). The sibling dispatcher on-board endpoint correctly fixes the cost at 12.

extra.message: issuePortalQuickAccess (and support-context) set the 'portalQuickAccess' cookie - which acts as an unauthenticated bearer capability for the anonymous GET /api/customers/portal-quick-access/context endpoint that returns customer data and jobs - without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes and with no expiration/TTL on the underlying session Map entry. The token is readable by client-side JS (XSS-stealable), transmittable over plain HTTP, and never expires, giving persistent unauthenticated access to a customer's job data if leaked.
